ei.subject: 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연)
ei.title: A Better Future for Coffee Waste

fullPassage:
Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms right in your home using spent coffee grounds? Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for growing mushrooms. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you get started. First, mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk container and make four small holes in the sides. Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark place with a temperature between 18 and 25°C, and place the container there for two to four weeks until the mixture turns completely white. When this happens, move the container to a bright area with indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are ready to be picked.

The famous German musician Johann Sebastian Bach once said, ‘Without my morning coffee, I’m just like a dried-up piece of goat.’ Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents walking around with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and Koreans made a significant contribution to this huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee. This means that every Korean adult drank an average of one cup of coffee every day throughout the year. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a daily necessity.

The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste each year.

So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the grounds contain valuable organic compounds and minerals, they are simply destroyed.

Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible, reducing waste and environmental costs.

An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. The farm produce can be used to create various food items, such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which are sold in the chain’s coffee shops. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both economically and environmentally.

Recycled coffee grounds have a wide range of uses, including coffee logs, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and reusable cups. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood. Fabric made from coffee grounds absorbs sweat, dries quickly, and provides UV protection. Reusable cups from coffee grounds not only have a visually appealing appearance but also preserve the taste of the coffee.

Korea has shown a growing interest in recycling spent coffee grounds in recent years. The government is taking steps toward the creation of a sustainable recycling system in the coffee industry, while companies are dedicating themselves to researching and developing new uses for coffee waste. By recycling materials such as coffee waste, individuals can also help protect the environment. With continued efforts, the recycling of used coffee grounds is expected to increase, encouraging more sustainable methods of enjoying coffee for years to come.

questions.passage: So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, __________ methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(break down)과 동시에 일어나는 부대상황/결과를 나타내는 분사구문 releasing이 적절하다. "분해되면서 메탄을 방출한다"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ releasing: 동시동작/결과 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① released: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ② release: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
❌ ④ to release: to부정사 → 동시동작 표현에 부적절
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작/결과): 주절, ~ing ... → 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작이나 결과

questions.passage: The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent __________ of as waste.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "with + 목적어 + 분사" 구문에서 99.8%가 버려지는 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 disposed가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② disposed: with + O + p.p.(수동) → "나머지가 폐기물로 버려지면서"
❌ ① disposing: 능동 → 나머지가 스스로 버리는 것이 아님
❌ ③ to dispose: to부정사 → with 구문에 부적절
❌ ④ disposes: 동사 원형 3인칭 → with 구문에서 동사 불가
det.tip: with + O + p.p.(수동): 목적어가 동작을 당하는 경우 과거분사 사용

questions.passage: The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, __________ they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 fertilizer companies(장소)를 수식하고, 뒤에 완전한 절(they are transformed)이 오므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ where: 장소 선행사(companies) + 완전한 절 → 관계부사
❌ ① which: 뒤에 완전한 절 → 관계대명사 부적절
❌ ② what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사 있으므로 불가
❌ ③ who: 사람 선행사용 → companies는 장소 개념
det.tip: 선행사(장소) + where + 완전한 절: 장소를 수식하는 관계부사

questions.passage: Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible, __________ waste and environmental costs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 앞 절(promotes the reuse)의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 현재분사 reducing이 적절하다. "자원의 재사용을 촉진하여, 그 결과 폐기물을 줄인다"
det.analysis:
✅ ② reducing: 결과를 나타내는 분사구문 (현재분사)
❌ ① reduces: 동사 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ③ reduced: 과거분사 → 수동/완료이나 주어가 능동적으로 줄이는 것
❌ ④ to reduce: to부정사 → 결과 분사구문에 부적절
❌ ⑤ reduce: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
det.tip: 결과 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → "그 결과 ~하다"

questions.passage: Some SCGs are ①<u>incinerated</u> instead of being buried, but this ②<u>releasing</u> a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options ③<u>takes</u> into account the potential value of coffee grounds.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② releasing → releases: 주어 this의 동사로 현재 시제 releases가 적절하다. 분사가 아니라 주절의 본동사가 필요한 자리이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② releasing(분사) → releases(본동사): "but this releases a lot of CO2" → but 뒤 주어 this의 동사 필요
✅ ① incinerated: 수동태 → "소각되다" 올바름
✅ ③ takes: neither of + 복수명사이지만 동사는 단수 일치 → 올바름
det.tip: 접속사(but) 뒤에 주어 + 동사 구조가 필요 → 분사(~ing)가 아닌 본동사 사용

questions.passage:
The famous German musician Johann Sebastian Bach once said, ‘Without my morning coffee, I’m just like a dried-up piece of goat.’ Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents walking around with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and Koreans made a significant contribution to this huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee. This means that every Korean adult drank an average of one cup of coffee every day throughout the year. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a daily necessity.

The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste each year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021" → ICO에 따르면 약 천만 톤 소비 = 일치
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 약 천만 톤 소비: 본문과 정확히 일치
❌ ① 0.2%가 사용 (10%가 아님)
❌ ② 매일 평균 한 잔 (두 잔이 아님)
❌ ④ 상당한 환경 비용이 발생한다고 명시
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 숫자와 핵심 단어를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: 한국인 성인은 매일 평균 두 잔의 커피를 마셨다.
ICO에 따르면 2020~2021년 사이 약 천만 톤의 커피가 소비되었다.
커피 폐기물은 환경에 아무런 영향을 주지 않는다.

questions.passage: So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the grounds contain valuable organic compounds and minerals, they are simply destroyed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "this releases a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton" → 소각 시 톤당 338kg의 CO2가 많이 발생한다. 따라서 "거의 발생하지 않는다"는 본문과 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 소각 시 CO2가 거의 발생하지 않는다 → "releases a lot of CO2"와 정반대
✅ ① "classified as general waste and sent to landfills" → 일치
✅ ② "approximately 25 times more potent than CO2" → 일치
✅ ④ "contain valuable organic compounds and minerals" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제: "거의 없다(barely)" vs "많이(a lot)" 같은 정도 표현에 주의

ch: 커피 찌꺼기는 일반 폐기물로 분류되어 매립지로 보내진다.
메탄은 CO2보다 약 25배 더 강력한 온실가스이다.
커피 찌꺼기를 소각하면 CO2가 거의 발생하지 않는다.
커피 찌꺼기에는 유기 화합물과 미네랄이 포함되어 있다.

questions.passage:
Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible, reducing waste and environmental costs.

An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. The farm produce can be used to create various food items, such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which are sold in the chain’s coffee shops. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both economically and environmentally.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 순환경제를 통한 커피 폐기물 재활용 사례 소개 → 커피 폐기물 재활용의 필요성과 사례를 알리기 위해
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 커피 폐기물 재활용 필요성과 사례: circular economy + 커피찌꺼기 재활용 과정 구체적 설명
❌ ① 역사/기원: 언급 없음
❌ ② 마케팅 전략: 본문의 주제가 아님
❌ ④ 생산 효율성: 재활용이 주제이지 생산이 아님
❌ ⑤ 소비 습관 비판: 비판이 아닌 해결책 제시
det.tip: 글의 목적: 전체 흐름(문제 제기 → 해결책 → 사례)에서 핵심 주장을 파악

ch: 커피 매출 증가를 위한 마케팅 전략을 제안하기 위해
커피 폐기물 재활용의 필요성과 사례를 알리기 위해
커피 농장의 생산 효율성을 높이기 위해

questions.passage: The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial __________, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste each year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 커피에 대한 사랑이 상당한 환경 비용을 수반한다는 내용. 추출 과정에서 폐기물이 발생하고, 99.8%가 폐기물로 버려진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ environmental cost: 폐기물 발생 + 99.8% 폐기 = 환경 비용
❌ ① economic benefit: 경제적 이익 → 문맥과 반대
❌ ② cultural tradition: 문화적 전통 → 폐기물과 무관
❌ ③ health improvement: 건강 개선 → 언급 없음
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 "as the extraction process generates significant waste"가 핵심 단서 → 환경 비용

questions.passage: Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through __________. A(n) __________ promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자원의 재사용을 촉진하고 폐기물과 환경 비용을 줄이는 것은 순환경제 조치(circular economy measures)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② circular economy measures: 자원 재사용 촉진 + 폐기물/환경비용 감소 = 순환경제
❌ ① waste reduction programs: 부분적으로 맞지만 "재사용 촉진"의 핵심 개념 부족
❌ ③ government subsidies: 정부 보조금 → 본문 맥락과 불일치
❌ ④ consumer boycotts: 소비자 불매운동 → 언급 없음
det.tip: 빈칸이 두 곳에 공통으로 들어갈 때, 두 문장 모두에 자연스러운 표현을 찾기

questions.passage: Recycled coffee grounds have a wide range of uses, including coffee logs, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and __________. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood. Fabric made from coffee grounds absorbs sweat, dries quickly, and provides UV protection. __________ from coffee grounds not only have a visually appealing appearance but also preserve the taste of the coffee.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 재활용 커피 찌꺼기의 용도 중 세 번째로 언급된 것이 재사용 컵(reusable cups)이며, 시각적으로 매력적이고 커피 맛을 보존한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reusable cups: 커피 찌꺼기 용도 3가지 중 하나 + "visually appealing + preserve taste"
❌ ② plastic bottles: 플라스틱 병 → 재활용 맥락에 반함
❌ ③ paper bags: 종이 봉투 → 커피 맛 보존과 무관
❌ ④ glass jars: 유리병 → 커피 찌꺼기로 만드는 것이 아님
det.tip: 빈칸 두 곳 공통: 첫 번째 빈칸은 열거, 두 번째 빈칸은 설명 → 두 곳 모두에 맞는 표현 선택

questions.passage: According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was __________ (consume) worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and Koreans made a significant contribution to this huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: consume(동사) → consumed(과거분사): "was + p.p." 수동태 구문. 커피가 소비되었다(수동)
det.analysis:
consume(동사) → consumed(과거분사)
was ______ : be + p.p. 수동태 → "소비되었다"
주어 coffee가 소비되는 대상이므로 수동태
det.tip: be동사 + p.p. = 수동태: 주어가 동작의 대상일 때 사용

questions.passage: The government is taking steps toward the creation of a __________ (sustain) recycling system in the coffee industry, while companies are dedicating themselves to researching and developing new uses for coffee waste.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: sustain(동사) → sustainable(형용사): 명사 recycling system을 수식하는 형용사가 필요. "지속 가능한 재활용 시스템"
det.analysis:
sustain(동사) → sustainable(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 recycling system(명사)을 수식하는 형용사 필요
sustainable recycling system = 지속 가능한 재활용 시스템
det.tip: sustain → sustainable / comfort → comfortable / value → valuable — -able 형용사 변환

questions.passage: So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 커피 찌꺼기가 매립지에서 분해될 때 방출되는 온실가스의 이름을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "releasing methane, a greenhouse gas" → 매립 시 방출되는 온실가스 = methane(메탄)
det.analysis:
매립지에서 분해(break down) → 방출(releasing) → methane
methane = CO2보다 약 25배 강력한 온실가스
det.tip: "본문에서 찾기" 유형: 한글 힌트의 키워드(온실가스)와 대응하는 영어 표현을 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 수거된 커피 찌꺼기를 가공할 때 제거하는 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "processed to remove impurities" → 가공 시 제거하는 것 = impurities(불순물)
det.analysis:
collect → process to remove impurities → dry out → sell

questions.passage: The famous German musician Johann Sebastian Bach once said, ‘Without my morning coffee, I’m just like a dried-up piece of goat.’ Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents walking around with a cup of coffee in hand. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a daily necessity.

questions.passage: Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms right in your home using spent coffee grounds? Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for growing mushrooms. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you get started. First, mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk container and make four small holes in the sides. Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark place with a temperature between 18 and 25°C, and place the container there for two to four weeks until the mixture turns completely white. When this happens, move the container to a bright area with indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are ready to be picked.
